disclaimer: NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Copyright and trademark status changes, varies by country, and is fact-specific. This registry is a research aid and a mechanical guard rail - it is not a clearance opinion. Verify before publishing anything commercial.

risk_tiers.folklore: No copyright ever attached - myth, fable, legend, folk tale. Lowest risk. Modern ADAPTATIONS of these are still protected.
risk_tiers.expired: Copyright has lapsed on the source work. Low risk, but adaptation-specific trademarks may still bite.
risk_tiers.version-locked: Only one specific early version is public domain. Later versions remain protected. Requires --ack-version.
risk_tiers.jurisdiction-locked: Public domain in some countries and not others. Requires --jurisdiction on the clear list.
risk_tiers.high-risk: Actively and aggressively trademarked by a living rights-holder. Blocked unless cleared.

characters.name: The Ant and the Grasshopper
characters.safe_version: The fable itself and its two figures. Any visual design is yours to invent.
traps: Disney's 1934 Silly Symphony version has its own protected designs - do not copy that grasshopper's look.
characters.dgd_fit: The cleanest fable for time-preference and why storing value across seasons is a design problem, not a moral one.

characters.name: The Tortoise and the Hare
characters.safe_version: The fable and its two figures. Invent your own designs.
traps: Avoid Warner Bros. Bugs Bunny / Cecil Turtle styling - that is protected.
characters.dgd_fit: The single best fit for the anti-speculation position. Lets you use degen energy as the hare WITHOUT selling a play.

characters.name: King Midas
characters.safe_version: The myth of the golden touch. Any design is yours.
characters.dgd_fit: Gold that cannot be used is not wealth. A direct route into money-as-a-tool rather than money-as-a-hoard.

characters.name: Icarus
characters.safe_version: The myth. Any design is yours.
characters.dgd_fit: Flying too close to the sun, for leverage and blow-up risk - without naming any token or predicting any price.

characters.name: Sisyphus
characters.safe_version: The myth. Any design is yours.
characters.dgd_fit: Running to stand still - the felt experience of currency debasement, told without conspiracy framing.

characters.name: The Three Little Pigs
characters.safe_version: The folk tale. Invent your own pig designs.
traps: Disney's 1933 Silly Symphony designs and its 'Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf' song are protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Straw, sticks and brick maps cleanly onto how monetary systems are built and what makes one hold up.

characters.name: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
characters.safe_version: The fable. Any design is yours.
characters.dgd_fit: Why credibility is the scarce good in crypto, and why claims need verifying. Good for a 'check the white paper' beat.

characters.name: Robinson Crusoe
characters.safe_version: Defoe's 1719 novel. Long out of copyright everywhere.
traps: Modern film adaptations have their own protected designs.
characters.dgd_fit: 'Crusoe economics' is a real teaching device - build money up from one person, then two, then a village. Excellent for first-principles explainers.

characters.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
characters.safe_version: Dickens' 1843 novella and its text.
traps: Disney's Scrooge McDuck is a separate, protected character - do not blend them.
Muppet/Disney film designs are protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Hoarding versus circulation - money that does not move does no work. Pairs with the supply-chain motif.

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.safe_version: The Conan Doyle canon. The final US copyrights lapsed in 2023, so the character is now clear in the US.
traps: The deerstalker and calabash pipe come from illustrators and stage tradition, not the text - they are widely used but check specific modern designs.
Do not borrow from BBC Sherlock, Guy Ritchie films, or Elementary - those are protected.
characters.dgd_fit: The natural host for 'check the claim' content - reading a white paper like evidence rather than taking it on faith.

characters.name: Captain Nemo
characters.safe_version: Verne's novels Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas (1870) and The Mysterious Island (1875).
traps: Disney's 1954 film design is protected.
Alan Moore's League of Extraordinary Gentlemen version is protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Built his own system rather than joining an existing one. Use for design/engineering explainers - avoid any anti-government framing.

characters.name: Alice
characters.safe_version: Carroll's 1865 and 1871 books, and the Tenniel illustrations.
traps: Disney's 1951 design - the specific blue dress and pinafore styling - is protected.
American McGee's Alice designs are protected.
characters.dgd_fit: A newcomer asking obvious questions nobody answers. Strong device for beginner explainers - the audience learns through her.

characters.name: Lemuel Gulliver
characters.safe_version: Swift's 1726 novel.
traps: Modern film adaptations have protected designs.
characters.dgd_fit: Scale as the whole point - big numbers made intuitive. Useful for supply and dilution explainers.

characters.name: Don Quixote
characters.safe_version: Cervantes' novel.
characters.dgd_fit: Charging windmills - chasing a story rather than a mechanism. Handle warmly, never mock the audience.

characters.name: Frankenstein's Creature
characters.safe_version: Mary Shelley's 1818 novel ONLY. In the book the Creature is articulate, yellow-skinned, with flowing black hair and watery eyes.
traps: FLAT HEAD, NECK BOLTS, GREEN SKIN and the grunting brute are Universal's 1931 film design and are protected. This is the single most-copied mistake.
Do not call the Creature 'Frankenstein' if you are leaning on film iconography.
characters.dgd_fit: Designing something you then cannot control. Use sparingly - the horror register fights the calm educational tone.

characters.name: Dorothy Gale
characters.safe_version: Baum's Oz novels ONLY. In the books the slippers are SILVER.
traps: RUBY SLIPPERS are MGM's 1939 film and are protected.
Judy Garland's specific look, the blue gingham styling and the film's Emerald City design are protected.
Some later Oz books by other authors may still be in copyright.
characters.dgd_fit: The man behind the curtain is a strong, non-conspiratorial way into 'who actually decides what money is worth'.

characters.name: Popeye
characters.safe_version: The 1929 Segar comic-strip Popeye ONLY, which entered the US public domain on 1 January 2025.
traps: SPINACH-DERIVED STRENGTH first appeared in 1931 and is NOT yet public domain.
The Fleischer cartoon designs and later King Features material are protected.
King Features maintains active trademarks.
characters.dgd_fit: Weak fit for monetary education, and the spinach trap makes him easy to get wrong. Prefer a fable.

characters.name: Tintin
characters.safe_version: The 1929 Le Petit Vingtieme strips, US only, from 1 January 2025.
traps: COPYRIGHTED IN THE EU UNTIL 2054. Short-form video does not respect borders - if your audience is global, treat Tintin as unavailable.
Moulinsart/Herge estate enforces aggressively.
Later albums remain protected everywhere.
characters.dgd_fit: Do not use. The jurisdiction split is unmanageable on platforms that distribute globally by default.

characters.name: Peter Pan
characters.safe_version: Barrie's novel and the first stage adaptation, US only.
traps: In the UK, Great Ormond Street Hospital holds a perpetual right granted by Barrie - licensing is required.
Disney's 1953 design is protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Weak thematic fit and a live UK problem. Not recommended.

characters.name: James Bond
characters.safe_version: Fleming's original text, CANADA ONLY, and only if produced and distributed there.
traps: Not public domain in the US, UK or EU.
MGM/Danjaq trademarks are enforced aggressively worldwide.
The gun-barrel sequence, 007 logo and film designs are all protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Do not use. The Canada-only carve-out cannot survive global short-form distribution.

characters.name: Mickey Mouse (Steamboat Willie)
characters.safe_version: ONLY the 1928 Steamboat Willie / Plane Crazy design - black-and-white, pie-eyes, no gloves, no modern proportions.
traps: Disney holds ACTIVE TRADEMARKS on Mickey as a brand identifier - these do not expire.
Any use that suggests affiliation with or endorsement by Disney is actionable regardless of copyright.
Red shorts, white gloves, modern eyes and modern proportions are all protected.
Using Mickey to promote a financial product is exactly the fact pattern Disney litigates.
characters.dgd_fit: Do not use. Highest-profile trademark holder in the world plus a crypto context is the worst combination available.

characters.name: Winnie-the-Pooh
characters.safe_version: Milne's 1926 text and E.H. Shepard's original line illustrations ONLY.
traps: THE RED SHIRT IS DISNEY'S and is protected.
Tigger first appeared in 1928 and entered the US public domain separately - check per character.
Disney holds active trademarks on Pooh as a brand.
Disney enforces aggressively.
characters.dgd_fit: Do not use. Disney trademark exposure in a financial context is not worth it.

characters.name: Betty Boop
characters.safe_version: Only the 1930 first-appearance version, public domain in the US from 1 January 2026. Note she debuted as a caricatured dog-eared character, not the later human design.
traps: Fleischer Studios and King Features run an extensive, actively enforced merchandising trademark programme.
The familiar later design is NOT the 1930 design.
Trademark litigation over Betty Boop has been repeated and well documented.
characters.dgd_fit: Do not use. Active merchandising trademark plus a financial context.

characters.name: Cthulhu
characters.safe_version: Lovecraft's pre-1930 stories.
traps: Chaosium and other publishers hold trademarks on specific game-related uses.
Later Mythos additions by other authors are protected.
characters.dgd_fit: Occasionally used for 'the system is too big to understand'. Use with care - the register is far from calm and educational, and Lovecraft's personal politics invite unwanted discussion.
